title: Finite condensed realization and native tensor normalization
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $X$ a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $D$ be a normalized native functor [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-normalized-functor]. Write $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, $C_E$ for the raw rational finite stage [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], $B_E$ for the bounded constructible condensed $E$ category [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], and $c_E:B_E\to B_\Omega$ for condensed scalar extension. Let $H$ be the actual derived equivalence obtained by native scalar forgetting and restriction along the composite of globalCoefficientIso [def-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-coefficient-construction] with the bounded-to-native coefficient isomorphism. There exist full faithful functors $F_E:C_E\to B_E$ and natural isomorphisms $\beta_h:F_E T^{\rm cond}_h\cong T^{\rm raw}_h F_L$ for every $h:E\subset L$. For every source pair $A=(E,A_E)$ there is $e_A:H(D.JA)\cong c_E(F_E A_E)$. Write $a_h:T^{\rm cond}_h c_L\cong c_E$ for the standard condensed tensor associator. For $A=(E,A_E)$, $B=(F,B_F)$, a common extension $M$ and $f:T^{\rm raw}_{E,M}A_E\to T^{\rm raw}_{F,M}B_F$, these comparisons satisfy $$H(D.J([M,f]))=e_A\,\bigl(a_{E,M}^{-1}\,c_M(\beta_{E,M}F_M(f)\beta_{F,M}^{-1})\,a_{F,M}\bigr)\,e_B^{-1}.$$ Composition is written from left to right and underlying ambient morphisms are understood. This asserts the finite realizations and their tensor normalization; it asserts no bijection on Hom sets of the common-stage category and no essential-image statement at $\Omega$.

proof.text: Use the explicitly constructed native condensed scalar equivalence and the unchanged comparison record, extracted into the data module. Both coefficient factors are actual isomorphisms; restriction and native scalar forgetting form the derived equivalence H.
Use the explicit finite condensed realization, its full and faithful instances, and its scalar comparison.

Obtain the normalized natural comparison on the integral source and its integral transition equation. Extend each natural iso uniquely through raw scalar localization. Every raw rational object has an underlying integral object, so the component formula transfers the transition equation directly.

Factor a common-stage representative as isoToStage, the stage inclusion of its arrow, and inverse isoToStage. Apply the functor, naturality of the extended comparison, and the transition equation. Cancel the invertible comparisons and expand the closure transition to obtain exactly the required tensor representative formula.
